label: Institution
name: Palace Theatre
summary:
The Palace Theatre in the West End of London, built in 1891 as the Royal English Opera House, is one of London's most historic and architecturally significant theatres, famous as the original home of The Phantom of the Opera (1986-2011, the longest-running musical in West End history) and subsequent major productions. Its ornate terracotta exterior on Cambridge Circus and its imposing red-velvet interior make it one of the most recognizable theatre buildings in the world.

The theatre was built by impresario Richard D'Oyly Carte (famous for the Gilbert and Sullivan partnership) to present serious English opera as an alternative to the Italian opera that dominated Victorian London. The opening production was Sullivan's Ivanhoe (1891), but D'Oyly Carte sold the building after financial failure; it was renamed Palace Theatre in 1911 and became a variety and musical hall venue. Sarah Bernhardt, Pavlova, and Marie Lloyd performed there in the variety era.

Andrew Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera ran at the Palace Theatre from 1986 until moving to His Majesty's Theatre in 2011 — its 9,887 performance London run made it the longest-running musical in West End history. Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, winner of the most Olivier Awards in history (9), opened at the Palace in 2016. The theatre was extensively renovated under its new owner, Nimax Theatres, to restore its Victorian grandeur.
